types.name: AuthorizationRequest
types.meaning: One internal trusted request containing a session identity, one required Permission, and a scope-evidence reference.
types.domain: Auth Foundation protected operations in this exact-match slice.

types.name: Session
types.meaning: A server-recognized session with status, expiry, active role identities, and authorization revision.
types.domain: Sessions resolvable by the authorization evaluator at one decision time.

types.name: Role
types.meaning: A role identity with a set of positive exact-match Permission grants.
types.domain: Roles returned by the complete authoritative resolver for the session authorization revision.

types.name: Permission
types.meaning: A value triple of resource, action, and scope.
types.domain: Exact-match positive permissions; no wildcard, hierarchy, or explicit DENY effect.

types.name: AuthorizationDecision
types.meaning: Exactly one result in the closed set {ALLOW, DENY}.
types.domain: The result of evaluating one AuthorizationRequest.

types.name: Instant
types.meaning: A totally ordered decision time used for session expiry.

types.name: AuthorizationRevision
types.meaning: A comparable identity for the authorization facts used by the session and authoritative resolver.
types.domain: The session and current authorization state for its user.

predicates.name: PermissionExactEqual(p1, p2)
predicates.meaning: p1.resource = p2.resource and p1.action = p2.action and p1.scope = p2.scope.

predicates.name: RequiredPermission(q)
predicates.meaning: The one exact Permission required by the protected operation represented by q.

predicates.name: DecisionTime(q)
predicates.meaning: The one explicit authorization evaluation instant carried by q's trusted evaluation context.

predicates.name: CurrentAuthorizationRevision(q)
predicates.meaning: The one current authoritative revision against which q is evaluated.

predicates.name: ResolvedSession(q, s)
predicates.meaning: Trusted server-side resolution maps q's session identity to server-recognized Session s.

predicates.name: ResolvedActiveRole(s, r)
predicates.meaning: r.role_id is active in s and r is the authoritative role definition for s.authorization_revision.
predicates.domain: Session x Role at the authorization decision revision.

predicates.name: Grants(r, p)
predicates.meaning: Permission p is a positive exact permission in role r's permission set.

predicates.name: SessionCurrent(s, decision_time, current_revision)
predicates.meaning: s.status = ACTIVE, decision_time is before s.expires_at, and s.authorization_revision = current_revision.

predicates.name: TrustedScopeEvidence(q)
predicates.meaning: Trusted application code resolved q.required_permission.scope from the protected operation and target, and q.scope_evidence_ref identifies that resolution.

predicates.name: RoleRelationComplete(s, current_revision)
predicates.meaning: ResolvedActiveRole contains every and only role active in s, with each complete authoritative role definition, at current_revision.

predicates.name: AuthorizationAdmissible(q, s, decision_time, current_revision)
predicates.meaning: ResolvedSession(q, s) holds and is unique for q; decision_time = DecisionTime(q); current_revision = CurrentAuthorizationRevision(q); SessionCurrent(s, decision_time, current_revision), TrustedScopeEvidence(q), and RoleRelationComplete(s, current_revision) all hold.
predicates.domain: AuthorizationRequest x Session x Instant x AuthorizationRevision.

predicates.name: Decision(q)
predicates.meaning: The unique AuthorizationDecision produced for q.

equality_rules: Permission equality is exact component equality over resource, action, and scope.
Resource, Action, Scope, SessionId, RoleId, UserId, and AuthorizationRevision use their declared exact typed equality; no coercion or wildcard expansion is permitted.
Two role or session records with different stable identities are not equal even if their other fields match.
quantifiers: The outer rule quantifies over every AuthorizationRequest in this bounded Auth Foundation model.
Each authorization branch existentially quantifies over exactly resolved Session values and authoritative Role and Permission values for the request revision.
Three identity-bearing existence constraints require an admissible exact-match request, an admissible no-match request, and an inadmissible request in the potential request model.
No closed-world claim is made about users, sessions, roles, or permissions outside the supplied interpretation environment.
time_model: Authorization is evaluated at one explicit decision_time. SessionCurrent is false when status is not ACTIVE, decision_time is not before expires_at, or the session authorization revision differs from the current authoritative revision.
currentness_rules: The session record, current authorization revision, authoritative role relation, and trusted scope evidence are evaluated for the same decision time.
A missing or stale role definition makes RoleRelationComplete and therefore AuthorizationAdmissible false; it is never treated as an empty-but-current grant set.
Changing the meaning, interpretation, proposition, assumptions, selected profile, or claim ceiling creates a new FormalClaim identity.
applicability: internal authorization after authentication has produced or resolved a server-recognized session
role-derived positive permissions with exact resource, action, and scope equality
trusted application construction of the required permission and scope evidence
assumptions: RoleRelationComplete is true only when the interpretation environment supplies every and only active authoritative role definition for the session authorization revision.
Role permission sets contain only positive grants; explicit DENY effects are absent from this claim.
The authorization decision codomain is exactly {ALLOW, DENY}, and evaluation is total for every in-scope request.
TrustedScopeEvidence is independently established before the authorization policy evaluates the permission match.
The formal claim models policy meaning, not how sessions, roles, revisions, or scope evidence are stored or transported.
excluded_cases: explicit DENY grants and deny precedence
wildcard, prefix, hierarchical, or subsumption permission matching
direct user permissions and role inheritance
ABAC, ReBAC, ownership, tenant fallback, and separation-of-duty policies
credential verification, token protocols, and authentication assurance
runtime completeness or correctness of the role resolver and scope-evidence producer
witnesses: A current ACTIVE session activates role billing-reader; that role grants Permission(invoice, read, tenant-7); the trusted request requires exactly that permission; Decision = ALLOW.
The same current session and role grant Permission(invoice, read, tenant-8) while the request requires tenant-7; Decision = DENY.
An expired or unresolved session makes AuthorizationAdmissible false even when some role definition would otherwise grant the required permission; Decision = DENY.
counterexamples: An always-ALLOW decision violates every no-match, stale-session, or untrusted-scope case.
An always-DENY decision violates the exact current active-role grant witness.
Treating a user-assigned but session-inactive role as active changes ResolvedActiveRole and violates the interpretation.
Treating a broader or wildcard scope as equal changes PermissionExactEqual and violates the interpretation.
vacuity_checks: At least one admissible exact-match ALLOW witness is required so the proposition cannot pass through an empty request or role universe.
At least one admissible no-match DENY witness is required so the proposition cannot be implemented as always ALLOW.
At least one inadmissible-session DENY witness is required so permission possession cannot bypass session currentness.
The interpretation must distinguish role assignment, session activation, permission grant, permission requirement, and decision.
claim_ceiling: Owner-accepted definitions-aligned InterpretationModel for one exact-match authorization policy. It exact-binds accepted BusinessMeaning v2, assumes rather than proves complete authoritative role resolution and trusted scope evidence, and establishes no FormalClaim admission, obligation, provider result, EVF result, runtime conformance, security, resilience, release, deployment, or production readiness.
